title: Google Pixel 11 Review Roundup: Worth the Price Rise?
description: Volt’s research-based verdict on the Google Pixel 11: the cameras, display and AI reviewers rate, against a higher price, middling speed and battery life.
intro: Google’s new mainstream Pixel is a refinement of last year’s phone with a higher price. Reviewers still rate it, with clear caveats.
verdict: A great everyday camera phone. A strong upgrade from older Pixels, not from a Pixel 10.
pros: Useful on-device AI features and clean software
cons: Costs more than the Pixel 10 did at launch
Performance trails rival flagships in benchmarks and gaming
An iterative update over last year’s model
bestFor: Owners of a Pixel 9 or older, and anyone who prioritises cameras and AI features over raw speed.
skipIf: You own a Pixel 10, or you play demanding games and want the longest battery life.
cardText: A great camera phone; upgrade from older Pixels, not a Pixel 10.

sections.html: Engadget scored it 9.2/10, calling it one of the best smartphones available but not worth upgrading to from a Pixel 10. Tom’s Guide was the most critical, pointing to the $100 price increase, flat battery life and small performance gains. Expert Reviews called it a great phone with a mediocre processor, praising the display and cameras. T3 called it an iterative update that still makes a great daily phone, and SlashGear was the most enthusiastic of all.

The consensus is clear: cameras, screen and AI features are the reasons to buy; price, speed and battery are the reasons to pause. If your current phone is a few years old, it’s a strong pick, especially on a launch or Black Friday deal. Browse more phones in the phones and wearables finder.
